comments.why: How regulation leads to centrally planned healthcare
comments.text: Careful, "for-profit" healthcare has a lot of government controls on it. Single payer is only obvious after you add a lot of controls to the market. See [LINK] and the more complete [VIDEO] . He explains how regulation eventually results in a centrally planned setup that is less efficient than what used to happen.

comments.story: The Moratorium on US Medical School Enrollment from 1980 to 2005 (2008)
comments.why: Friedman on protecting against quacks without licensing limits
comments.text: For any interested, here[1] is the late Milton Friedman's take on how we might protect against quacks, frauds, and snake-oil salesmen posing as doctors if government didn't step in to limit the supply of medical doctors in the name of quality control. I realize it's not exactly what the article is discussing, but it's certainly relevant for all the same reasons. This is during the Q&A of his lecture "The Economics of Medical Care", given to the very people who would most object to his ideas: [1] [VIDEO]
